offers.name: ASUS Vivobook 16 16" 60Hz Laptop - AMD Ryzen 5 3501U - 16GB DDR4 RAM - 256GB SSD - Windows 11 Home - Cool Silver

praises: 16-inch 1920x1200 panel at this price is a lot of screen, and 300 nits beats the 15.6" Vivobook's 250
16GB DDR4 in a SO-DIMM slot — genuinely upgradeable, unlike soldered rivals
USB-C supports power delivery and DisplayPort: one cable for charging and an external monitor
1080p webcam is a step up from the 720p units on the Vivobook 15
Mendocino sips power: quiet, cool, and the best battery of the x86 Vivobooks
complaints: 256GB SSD fills almost immediately — Windows plus a year of photos and it is tight
Ryzen 5 3501U is a 4-core/4-thread Zen 2 design from 2021; heavy multitasking stutters
No keyboard backlight, no webcam privacy shutter
1.75 kg makes it the heaviest Vivobook here despite the thin look
Plastic chassis flexes in the deck; hinge is middling like the rest of the line

standouts: Only 16" FHD+ panel in this budget family, with USB-C PD+DP and upgradeable RAM
design_philosophy: Screen-first budgeting: ASUS puts the biggest display of its budget range on the cheapest serious CPU it can source — a 4-thread Zen 2 refresh — and pads with 16GB DDR4. The bet is that buyers scrolling BestBuy filter on "16-inch, 16GB"; the trade-offs (256GB SSD, 4 threads, older silicon) are hidden in the spec sheet. The working USB-C PD/DP port is a real, if quiet, plus.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-vivobook.md). Platform-anchored on Mendocino (4C/4T Zen 2, Radeon 610M): productivity 4.9 despite 16GB — 4 threads is the ceiling; gaming 1.5. Battery estimated from ~50 Wh + very efficient SoC. BBY lists aspect as 16:9 — spec error; 1920x1200 is 16:10. Image URL best-guess BBY CDN pattern.
